newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish poll finds growing support for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Swedish poll finds growing support for EMU.

text.p: The majority of Swedes want to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), according to an opinion poll, released on Monday, that confirmed Swedish support for EMU is growing.
The Swedish Gallup poll, published in tabloid newspaper Expressen, found 52 percent of the 1,000 Swedes surveyed wanted Sweden to join EMU.
Of them 26 percent wanted Sweden to join EMU from the start on January 1, 1999 and 26 percent wanted membership at a later date.
The poll found 37 percent of interviewees wanted Sweden to stay outside the monetary union.
Sweden's minority Social Democratic government has yet to clarify its position on Sweden's EMU membership.
The party leaders are to make their recommendation in June this year which will be put to the party's congress that starts on September 8 for a final decision.
A poll by pollster Skop on April 1 found almost one in five Swedes, or 19 percent, wanted to be in the first wave of countries to join EMU in 1999.
A total of 55 percent of respondents wanted to wait-and-see how EMU developed before making a firm decision or were uncertain while the rest said a flat no to membership.
In January 23 percent of people surveyed were in favour of joining EMU at the start compared to 18 percent in a similar survey last November.
The January poll found 23 percent thought Sweden should join EMU at a later stage while 39 percent were opposed and the rest undecided.
